submission.justification: Simulated energy resolution at 662 keV (FWHM, 100k events per point) for all three candidates across thicknesses: K3 is best at every thickness (2 cm 3.25%, 4 cm 3.05%, 5 cm 2.98%, 6 cm 2.96%, 10 cm 3.90%); K2 best 4.45% at 5 cm; K1 best 8.51% at 5 cm. K3 at 5-6 cm is the minimum; resolution is flat within 5-6 cm, so 6 cm is the lowest measured point. CAVEAT: the hard intrinsic-background constraint (100-3000 keV <= 0.5 counts/kg/day) cannot be verified with the tools or project documents. No document or tool reports intrinsic background for any candidate. K3 is described as high light yield and fast decay, which is the profile of LaBr3-type scintillators that can carry intrinsic radioactivity in this energy window, so K3 is the candidate most at risk of failing the budget. The recommendation is conditional: K3 at 6 cm should be adopted only after a measured or certified intrinsic background (100-3000 keV) below 0.5 counts/kg/day is confirmed. If K3 fails, K2 (4.45% at 5 cm) is the next-best option, subject to the same check.

requirements.requirement: Crystal must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 662 keV

requirements.requirement: Intrinsic background (100-3000 keV) must not exceed 0.5 counts/kg/day (hard requirement)
requirements.evidence: No tool or document provides intrinsic background for any candidate. The simulation tool only returns resolution. Must be verified before adoption; K3 is a plausible risk given its LaBr3-like profile.
